title: Standard Cost Model (SCM) API — PRD tracking + cross-functional sign-off
creator: Talia Benson
description:
## Summary
This ticket tracks completion of the Standard Cost Model (SCM) PRD and required cross-functional sign-offs. SCM standardizes how Redwood models and exposes inference cost so that Console (cost breakdown + transparency) and Optimize (batching/caching/quantization recommendations) operate on consistent, auditable economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

This PRD is *not* a billing/pricing engine and does *not* change invoices in the initial release. It is a technical cost attribution + estimation spec with deterministic API outputs.

## Problem
Today, cost computations and breakdowns are inconsistent across surfaces:
- Console cost views rely on a mix of metering, heuristics, and per-team logic, making breakdowns hard to explain.
- Optimize “what-if” recommendations can’t reliably compare scenarios across regions/hardware because inputs/assumptions differ.
- Runtime telemetry emits useful signals, but not always in normalized/consistent units, and dimensionality can be lost in pipelines.

Outcome: customers and internal teams see discrepancies and can’t easily audit why cost changed (batching enabled, cache warmed, quant profile changed, etc.).

## Goals (v1)
1) Define and publish a Standard Cost Model spec (SCM v1)
- Canonical inputs, outputs, units, semantics.
- Deterministic results (same inputs => same outputs).
- Explicit assumptions and confidence semantics.

2) Ship a versioned Cost Model API used by:
- Console: per-route/model breakdown panels + tooltips.
- Optimize: scenario sweeps (“what-if”) for batching/caching/quant profile candidates.

3) Align runtime telemetry with SCM
- Ensure signals exist for attribution and that tagging rules support explainability without exploding cardinality.

4) Guardrails
- Backward compatibility policy + version negotiation.
- Validation rules for required/optional fields.
- Audit logging for reads of customer-level cost data.
- SLOs appropriate to Console dependency criticality.

## Non-goals (v1)
- Changing customer invoices or contract pricing logic.
- Full discounting/contract/pricing engine.
- Perfect cost accounting for every edge case; v1 must be explainable and robust with confidence signals when inputs are missing.

## Target users
- Internal: Console engineering + PM (Marissa), Optimize engineering + PM (Aditya), Platform/Control Plane (Priya/Ethan), Runtime (Mateo/Sofia/Omar), Telemetry (Logan/Nadia), SRE (Sean/Rafael), Security (Dr. Aisha Rahman/Kevin Osei).
- External (indirect): customers viewing Console cost breakdown and customers benefiting from Optimize cost reduction recommendations.

## Key user stories
Console
- As a customer, I can see total cost and a breakdown that is consistent across regions and deployments.
- As Support/CS, I can explain why cost changed (e.g., cache miss vs hit, batching efficiency shift) without guessing.

Optimize
- As an engineer, I can run “what-if” comparisons: batching on/off, cache warm/cold, quant profile swap, and see cost deltas + confidence.
- As Optimize, I can block or down-rank recommendations when confidence is low or assumptions are too strong.

## Requirements (PRD-level)
### API behavior
- Endpoints:
  - `POST /cost-model/estimate` (pure estimate based on inputs + tables)
  - `POST /cost-model/explain` (estimate + breakdown + contributing factors and assumptions)
- Version negotiation: client specifies required/acceptable versions; server responds with selected version and compatibility metadata.
- Determinism: no nondeterministic dependencies (e.g., time-varying tables) without explicit version pinning.
- Strict input validation:
  - If required inputs missing: return structured error.
  - If optional signals missing: compute with explicit assumptions and reduced confidence.

### Output schema (high-level)
- Total cost (single currency unit + internal “compute unit” normalization)
- Breakdown by cost component (compute, memory, cache efficiency, overhead)
- Confidence score + confidence reasons
- Assumptions list (human-readable + machine-readable codes)
- Attribution vs estimate: v1 supports both semantics via clear fields and documentation.

### Telemetry alignment (v1)
Required or strongly recommended signals (tagged with model/version, region, hardware sku where available):
- Prefill vs decode token counts and time
- Batch size effective + batch efficiency
- KV-cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache) and warm/cold context
- Quantization profile id
- Deployment mode: hosted/dedicated/private

### Reliability
- SLOs defined and alerted on:
  - Availability (monthly) and p95/p99 latency (regional)
  - Error rate by error class (validation vs internal failures)
- Caching strategy must not break determinism. Memoization allowed only when it does not change results.

### Security/compliance
- Audit log events for any request returning tenant/customer cost breakdown.
- RBAC: restrict access to customer cost breakdown endpoints based on internal roles/service identities.
- Redaction guidance for sensitive fields (e.g., actor identifiers) in logs.

## Success metrics
Adoption
- Console uses SCM for cost breakdown for >= 90% of tenants in rollout cohorts within 2 weeks of GA.
- Optimize “what-if” sweeps consume SCM outputs for >= 90% of candidate evaluations in production.

Quality
- Determinism: 0 mismatches for identical input payloads in regression suite.
- Explainability: 100% of responses include either (a) full signal coverage or (b) explicit assumptions + confidence reasons.
- Drift monitoring: canary comparing SCM estimates vs metered attribution alerts if median absolute % error exceeds 10% on fixed prompt set (per model family), sustained 30 min.

Performance
- `estimate` endpoint p95 <= 150 ms and p99 <= 400 ms (regional), excluding client network.
- `explain` endpoint p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 600 ms.

Reliability
- Availability >= 99.9% monthly (subject to dependency criticality for Console; error budget policy in SLO doc).
- Console fallback behavior: if SCM unavailable/slow, page degrades gracefully (cached data or “unavailable” state) without blocking critical navigation.

## Milestones (tracked here for PRD sign-off; engineering tickets track implementation)
1) Discovery + alignment complete
- Confirmed primary use-cases (Console breakdown, Optimize what-if)
- Telemetry gap list agreed

2) PRD + spec complete
- SCM v1 spec drafted, reviewed, and signed off
- Versioning/negotiation ADR approved

3) Implementation underway
- Cost Model service skeleton
- Runtime instrumentation + telemetry pipelines

4) Integrations
- Console wiring + UX copy
- Optimize scenario sweep integration + guardrails

5) Launch
- Canary and staged rollout by tenant/tier
- Dashboards + alerts
- Support enablement + documentation

## Dependencies and owners (high level)
- Schema/spec: Jordan Lee (Eng), Aditya Rao (PM), Marissa Cole (PM)
- Service + control plane integration: Priya Natarajan / Ethan Park
- Runtime signals: Mateo Alvarez / Sofia Ivanova / Omar El-Sayed
- Telemetry pipeline: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman / Thomas Baird
- Console integration: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin / Jada Williams
- Optimize integration: Hassan Mirza / Yara Haddad
- SLO/alerts: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Security review + audit logs: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Kevin Osei

## Risks / open issues (tracked until sign-off)
- Cardinality pressure if we tag too many dimensions (model version x route x tenant x region x sku). Mitigation: aggregation strategy + limits; preserve explainability via assumptions and limited dimensions.
- Missing telemetry during rollouts/restarts can reduce confidence and confuse customers. Mitigation: explicit assumptions in payload + Console copy and tooltips.
- Confusion between “estimate” and “metered attribution.” Mitigation: explicit naming in API and UI (“Estimated cost”) + docs.

## Sign-off checklist
Required approvals for PRD completion:
- Product: Aditya Rao, Marissa Cole
- Platform/Control plane: Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez
- Telemetry: Logan Wright
- SRE: Sean Gallagher
- Security/compliance: Dr. Aisha Rahman (audit + access controls)
- Unit economics: Laura Bennett (sanity check on cost component definitions)

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (PM-482)
- PRD in Confluence is up to date and matches v1 scope.
- Links to SCM spec + ADR included.
- Stakeholders listed above have commented approval or are explicitly marked “FYI/no objections.”
- Milestones and success metrics agreed and reflected in engineering tickets.
comments: 2025-01-27 (Talia Benson): Created tracking ticket for SCM PRD completion + sign-off. Kicking off discovery notes collection across Console/Optimize/Platform/Runtime.

2025-01-30 (Marissa Cole): Console needs a stable breakdown schema + tooltips for assumptions. Please ensure `explain` includes fields we can map to UI sections without additional joins. Also: we should label as “Estimated cost” in v1 to reduce billing confusion.

2025-02-02 (Logan Wright): Telemetry gap: kv-cache hit-rate tags are not consistent across runtime versions; also prefill/decode split is not emitted everywhere. We can get there but need strong cardinality rules early.

2025-02-04 (Mateo Alvarez): Runtime can emit prefill/decode and batch_efficiency with low overhead if we avoid per-token tagging. Sampling acceptable for some series, but SCM should treat missing data explicitly (assumptions).

2025-02-06 (Jordan Lee): Version negotiation: recommend header-based required/acceptable semantics with server-selected version echoed in response. Adding compatibility tests to avoid breaking older Console clients.

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): SLO targets need to be explicit: Console cost breakdown is user-facing but should degrade gracefully. We should not page SRE for transient validation errors; alert on internal error rate + latency.

2025-02-13 (Aditya Rao): PRD ready for sign-off. Key constraints emphasized: deterministic outputs, explicit assumptions/confidence, and no billing changes in v1. Requesting security + unit economics sanity review before marking Done.

2025-02-14 (Dr. Aisha Rahman): Security review notes: cost breakdown is customer-sensitive in some contexts. Audit logs required for reads; ensure service-to-service authz is least-privilege; avoid logging full request payloads in plaintext.

2025-02-18 (Laura Bennett): Unit economics review: component taxonomy is reasonable for v1. Strongly recommend keeping “overhead” as a separate component to avoid hiding platform costs inside compute.
2025-03-03 (Talia Benson): All required sign-offs captured in threads; PRD/spec/ADR links updated in ticket. Marking Done.
